_comment: Vendored reference bytes for tests/tools-parity-test.sh. Each entry records the historical vault path and the exact commit the bytes were extracted from, via: git show <commit>:<historical_path> > tests/fixtures/tool-parity-ref/<file>, followed by any redactions listed below. The historical path predates the 2026-09-09.1 rename and uses the pre-rename `corp-sdd-starter` tree on purpose — see tools-parity-test.sh's KIT_PREFIX comment. `original_sha256` is the checksum of the RAW historical bytes exactly as git history holds them, before any redaction. `sha256` is the checksum of the vendored file exactly as it sits in this directory (no trailing-newline games) — the bytes on disk, after every redaction in `redactions` has been applied to the historical bytes. `redactions` is an ordered list of exact, literal find/replace pairs; each `find` must occur EXACTLY ONCE in the historical bytes, applied in list order. A file that was vendored byte-for-byte carries an empty `redactions` list and `original_sha256 == sha256`. tools-parity-test.sh's verify-vendor-drift check recomputes `sha256` against the vendored file on disk and, when this vault's git history is present, also re-derives the commit via the same resolve_ref_commit walk the suite always used, hashes the raw historical bytes against `original_sha256`, applies `redactions` to those bytes, and diffs the result against `sha256` — so a reader (or the gate) can re-derive the vendored file from history plus this record, exactly.

redactions.replace: // repo identity is committed data, not the folder name (CI workspaces, worktrees, renamed clones)
redactions.reason: a customer-technology noun was redacted from a vendored comment before this fixture directory became public. The original text is identified by line number and hash, NOT quoted: quoting it here would republish the very noun the redaction removes. Anyone holding this vault's history can re-derive it from the recorded commit and path. The comment is prose only, so the parity gate still measures the same behavioural contract (exit code, stdout, stderr).
